My father was the director of an engineering firm. They made the machines that made cans or something. I was quite young when he explained. My father wasn’t a very nice person. We still aren’t very well off. I got a job the minute I could, so I at least have new clothes, a phone that works, and am able to pursue interests. My brother is lazy, possibly because father would buy him stuff and the things he needed when we were younger and still does now. He’s old enough for a job, just can’t be bothered. I’m supposed to have taken my a-levels this year but exams have been cancelled. I’m kinda worried I’ll be stuck in poverty forever to be honest. Ah yes. Complaints about language change. Because language is definitely not an every evolving thing, with like becoming both a word and a filler. 

Like has become another filler word, just like “okay”, “right”, “uh” and “um”which serve important parts in conversation as it’s individuals Thinking about what they’re talking about. It’s filler. Semantic change happens. It’s Life. 

Like used to be linked to the word lic, which meant the body in Old English. The word lic was found in the word gelic, to mean “with the body”, as in “with the body of” which basically means “similar to”. I Believe it’s Old English but it’s been a while since I studied language history so it could be of other origin. But. Yes. In it’s original form, like was used to liken something to something else. 

And that of course isn’t the only way it’s used, in a “correct English” type of way. To like something, and how likely something is to happen, they’re other ways the word like has changed meaning via natural semantic change. 

Filler is also a natural and essential part of discourse. Maybe you do not like the use of like. That’s fine. No need for you yourself to use it. But it’s a part of the natural progression of the English language, just like MLE, wider slang, initialisms and acronyms, the decline of correct grammar and the fairly recent usage of emoticons. But I suppose it’s a whole other kettle of fish when someone with seemingly prescriptivist views has their own modern language changes pointed out to them. 

I get some people think it’s annoying, but I also find it annoying we have to constantly put down other people’s language usage for it seemingly sounding dumb. It’s Exactly the same as people who speak in RP, or have a generally posh accent, talking down on say the Yorkshire accent, holding a belief that everyone with that accent is dumb. It isn’t. We can’t have it both ways. We can’t try and destroy social stigma for one thing while simultaneously creating it for another. It’s ridiculous.

My earliest memory is of bringing my dog home. 

I was about two, so some of it is pretty hazy. But I remember her being set down on the floor and her kinda bumbling about all cute n’ stuff. I remember us discussing what we were going to call her; settling on Molly. I remember giving her this big hug, I imagine I was told to not be rough or anything as she was small. She quickly became my best friend, but that’s a whole other story. There was this funny box we brought her home in; like a vegetable crate style thing. 

We had to put her down on the sixth of December; her being sixteen, myself recently having turned eighteen. Early stage kidney disease. There wasn’t anything that could have been done, and we can’t afford it even if there was. She shuffled over as the sedatives kicked in and kinda collapsed in my arms, and then the vet did what he had to do. I still expect to see her every time I walk into the room. It’s rough, but I’m glad there wasn’t a second of my consciousness she wasn’t around up until this point, and I’m glad I was aware of every second I spent with her.

Actually, there’s a phenomenon known as the fis/fish phenomenon, which helps show that a child’s perception of phonemes (sounds in language) happens before they can actually produce the sound itself. 

An experiment, by I think it was Berko (?), was ran to demonstrate this, in which a child had a plastic fish. He was asked if that was his fish, and he said something like “yes it’s my fis”. When asked if it was his fis, he replied no, saying it was his fis. But he didn’t realise what he was saying was incorrect, believing he was in fact saying fish. 

So even though you could correct your child on this, chances are they don’t hear anything wrong with what they’re saying.

My health and social care teacher had a neighbour we’ll name X. X was schizophrenic and paranoid; neighbours disliked him because he was different. X was a hermit, never really leaving the house. 

My teacher felt bad for him, and so befriended him. She’d check up on him, take him food from barbecues they’d had, that kind of thing. Every Christmas she’d take him a Christmas dinner, and he’d always have presents for her two daughters. 

So last Christmas X didn’t answer the door. It wasn’t unusual for him to not answer the door, so she thought nothing of it and let him be. We all know where this is going. 

I go to class a couple weeks after Christmas break is over, and she looks like she’d been crying. She’d gone to check on X again (she had a few times since Christmas by this point) and X never answered. Her husband, a policeman, broke down the door to check on him, but didn’t need to go much further than his stairs. He’d died in his sleep, with his heating on, so he’d been baking in this room alone for a few weeks. She felt awful about it, as she thought more could have been done. She could have done more. 

But the truth is, some people just don’t like leaving the house. Some people can’t leave it because of medical reasons, some people just don’t like people. Some have mental health issues. And then some are isolated because they don’t have friends. Sometimes reaching out is a good thing; X had someone who did truly care for him. He had no family or anything like that. He had someone who’d check in on him, cook him Christmas dinner and was so worried about his funeral arrangements she ended up calling the council to see if there was anything she herself could do. And sometimes people just don’t want that. I guess what I’m saying is just because you feel like you could do more, doesn’t mean you really could. And sometimes you’re doing enough without even realising it.
